headline: Microsoft pauses Office update after license deactivations, cause unconfirmed
summary: Microsoft paused its KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update after users reported it deactivated or removed perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations. One outlet reports Microsoft has not confirmed the update actually caused the license deactivations, framing responsibility for the bug as still unresolved.

claims.statement: A Windows update deactivated or removed some users' perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations.

sources.quote: it deactivated, or in some cases completely removed, perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations
Office 2016 and 2019 holdouts blame update for license deactivation bug

claims.statement: Microsoft paused the rollout of the KB5002907 update in response.

sources.quote: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations

discrepancies.explanation: One outlet treats the update as the cause of the deactivations, while the other notes Microsoft has not confirmed the update was at fault.

quotes.quote: Microsoft has paused the rollout of the KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update after users report that it deactivated
But was the update at fault? Microsoft isn't saying
